vintagewatercolor.gen_prompt: Create a collectible vintage tourism poster for this city, in the style of classic 1920s-1950s European travel advertising printed on aged paper. DECORATIVE BORDER, follow this exactly: a plain flat cream margin of about 4 percent of the image width runs around all four edges, exactly the same thickness on top, bottom, left and right. Just inside that margin sits a thin dark keyline frame with small ornate gold filigree flourishes in each of the four corners. Because the canvas is 2 units wide and 3 units tall, the frame is also 2 units wide and 3 units tall, a scaled down copy of the canvas shape. The entire illustration and all lettering stay fully inside this frame. The margin outside the frame is plain untextured cream with no illustration, no text and no extra lines. TITLE: the city name in very large elegant serif display capitals, deep navy blue with a subtle thin lighter inline outline, spanning almost the full width of the frame, set at the very top against open sky. Nothing may overlap or obscure the lettering: keep foliage, branches, rooftops and birds clear of it. TAGLINE: directly beneath the title, one short evocative tagline of three to five words about this specific city, in smaller letterspaced serif capitals, flanked left and right by small ornamental dividers. SCENE: a richly detailed scenic collage of the city's most iconic landmarks, architecture, monuments and recognizable local elements. The main landmark sits prominently in the middle distance, with smaller architectural and cultural details layered around it. FOREGROUND: the viewer looks out over the city from an elevated vantage point such as a cafe terrace, a quayside, a balcony, a stone staircase or a railing, framed by flowers and foliage in the lower corners. Anchor this vantage point with quiet objects rather than crowds: a small cafe table with two chairs, a lantern, a moored boat, a tram, a market stall or potted plants. PEOPLE: include a human figure ONLY when this city has a distinctive, instantly recognizable traditional dress or cultural figure that genuinely adds local character, for example a kimono in Kyoto. If the city has no such distinctive dress, show no people at all and let the empty terrace or quayside carry the scene. Never add generic modern strolling figures or crowds. MIDGROUND: the streets, water, bridges or plazas the city is known for. BACKGROUND: the skyline, hills or coastline, with a soft glowing sun and dreamy layered clouds. PALETTE: warm, nostalgic and slightly faded. Soft pastel blue, peach, coral, terracotta, cream, golden yellow, turquoise and sage green, muted rather than bright, as if the inks have aged. STYLE: hand-painted lithograph travel poster, whimsical storybook aesthetic, soft painterly textures, visible paper grain and subtle halftone print texture, charming miniature details, intricate but cohesive, strong foreground-midground-background depth. AVOID: photorealism, modern minimalist design, 3D rendering, distorted architecture, clutter, blurry details, landmarks that do not belong to this city. Absolutely no banner, cartouche, label, ribbon, plaque or text box at the bottom of the poster. No country name anywhere. No coordinates, no captions, no dates, no extra text of any kind apart from the title and the tagline.
